headline: Alaska Native village corporations no longer must give land to the state to hold for future town governments, and can reclaim such land.
what_it_does: Under the Alaska Native Claims Settlement Act, village corporations that received land had to give some of it to the local town government, or to the State of Alaska to hold in trust if no town government existed yet. This law ends the requirement to give land to the state in trust for a future town government. It also lets village corporations get back land the state already holds in trust, if both the village corporation and the village's residents formally vote to end the trust.

who_it_affects.how: They no longer have to transfer land to the state for future town governments and can regain title to land already held in trust.

who_it_affects.group: Residents of Alaska Native villages without a town government
who_it_affects.how: They must take part in a formal resolution, together with the village corporation, for trust land to be returned to the corporation.
It will no longer receive this land in trust and may lose land it currently holds in trust if villages dissolve those trusts.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted July 7, 2025; the summary does not give a separate start date.
